text:
Accelerometers are increasingly used to obtain valuable descriptors of physical activity for health research. The cut-points approach to segment accelerometer data is widely used in physical activity research but requires resource expensive calibration studies and does not make it easy to explore the information that can be gained for a variety of raw data metrics. To address these limitations, we present a data-driven approach for segmenting and clustering the accelerometer data using unsupervised machine learning.

The data used came from five hundred fourteen-year-old participants from the Millennium cohort study who wore an accelerometer (GENEActiv) on their wrist on one weekday and one weekend day. A Hidden Semi-Markov Model (HSMM), configured to identify a maximum of ten behavioral states from five second averaged acceleration with and without addition of x, y, and z-angles, was used for segmenting and clustering of the data. A cut-points approach was used as comparison.

Time spent in behavioral states with or without angle metrics constituted eight and five principal components to reach 95% explained variance, respectively; in comparison four components were identified with the cut-points approach. In the HSMM with acceleration and angle as input, the distributions for acceleration in the states showed similar groupings as the cut-points categories, while more variety was seen in the distribution of angles.

Our unsupervised classification approach learns a construct of human behavior based on the data it observes, without the need for resource expensive calibration studies, has the ability to combine multiple data metrics, and offers a higher dimensional description of physical behavior. States are interpretable from the distributions of observations and by their duration.

Unsupervised machine learning, specifically a Hidden Semi-Markov Model (HSMM), was applied to raw accelerometer data from 514 participants in the Millennium cohort study, who wore a GENEActiv device on their wrist for a weekday and a weekend day. Data consisted of five-second averaged acceleration readings, optionally supplemented with x, y, and z angular components. The HSMM was configured to detect up to ten behavioral states, enabling segmenting and clustering of activity without requiring pre-established cut-points or calibration studies.

In this methodology, eight principal components—derived from time spent in identified behavioral states and incorporating angle metrics—explained 95% of the variance in the acceleration signal, compared to four components when using a conventional cut-points approach. The cut-points method produced fewer, more simplified categories, whereas the HSMM approach yielded more nuanced distributions for both acceleration and angular data. Notably, the acceleration distributions in the unsupervised states mirrored the groupings found by the cut-points method, but with richer variation in angular data distributions.

The data-driven HSMM provided a higher-dimensional characterization of physical behavior by combining multiple sensor measurements and revealing distributions interpretable via state durations and observation patterns. This unsupervised method eliminated the need for resource-intensive calibrations while offering interpretable, multi-metric insights into human movement patterns from raw accelerometer data.

Accelerometers are widely applied to derive valuable descriptors of physical activity in health research. This unsupervised method learns behavioral constructs directly from the data, eliminating the need for costly calibration and enabling multi-variable analysis. It yields richer, high-dimensional descriptions of physical behavior, with state definitions accessible through observable distributions and durations.

text:
Forest fires in South Asia lead to widespread haze, where many healthy individuals develop psychosomatic symptoms. We investigated the effects of haze exposure on cerebral hemodynamics and new symptoms. We hypothesised that vasoactive substances present in the haze, would lead to vasodilation of cerebral vasculature, thereby altering cerebral hemodynamics, which in turn may account for new psychosomatic symptoms.

Seventy-four healthy volunteers were recruited, and serial transcranial Doppler (TCD) ultrasonography was performed to record blood flow parameters of bilateral middle cerebral arteries (MCA). The first TCD was performed in an air-conditioned environment. It was repeated outdoors after the participants spent 30-minutes in the haze environment. The prevailing level of pollutant standards index (PSI) was recorded. Appropriate statistical analyses were performed to compare cerebral hemodynamics at baseline and after haze exposure in all participants. Subgroup analyses were then employed to compare the findings between symptomatic and asymptomatic participants.

Study participants’ median age was 30 years (IQR 26–34), and new psychosomatic symptoms were reported by 35 (47.3%). There was a modest but significant decrease in pulsatility index (PI) and resistivity index (RI) in the left MCA after haze exposure (PI: p = 0.026; RI: p = 0.021). When compared to baseline parameters, haze exposure resulted in significantly lower mean PI (p = 0.001) and RI (p = 0.001) in symptomatic patients, but this difference was not present in asymptomatic patients (PI: p = 0.919; RI: p = 0.970).

Haze causes significant alterations in cerebral hemodynamics in susceptible individuals, probably responsible for various psychosomatic symptoms. The prognostic implications and health effects of haze require evaluation in a larger study.

text: Haze generated by forest fires in South Asia is associated with changes in cerebral hemodynamics among susceptible individuals. In this study, seventy-four healthy participants underwent serial transcranial Doppler ultrasonography of the bilateral middle cerebral arteries before and after a 30-minute exposure to ambient haze, measured by a pollutant standards index (PSI). Cerebral hemodynamics, assessed via pulsatility index (PI) and resistivity index (RI), were compared at baseline and after exposure. Statistically significant reductions in PI and RI were observed in the left middle cerebral artery following haze exposure (PI: p = 0.026; RI: p = 0.021). However, this reduction was only evident in individuals who developed new psychosomatic symptoms (PI: p = 0.001; RI: p = 0.001), while asymptomatic individuals showed no significant changes (PI: p = 0.919; RI: p = 0.970). These findings suggest that exposure to haze may be linked to cerebral vasodilation and altered hemodynamics in those prone to psychosomatic symptoms, potentially explaining their emergence. Further investigation with larger cohorts is needed to assess clinical implications.

Forest fires in South Asia generate widespread haze, during which many healthy individuals report psychosomatic symptoms. In this study, we examined how exposure to haze affects cerebral hemodynamics, hypothesizing that vasoactive compounds in the haze might induce cerebral vasodilation and consequently alter brain blood flow. 

We measured cerebral hemodynamics via serial transcranial Doppler ultrasound in the bilateral middle cerebral arteries of seventy-four healthy participants. Baseline scans were taken indoors, followed by a repeat in a haze environment where the pollutant standards index (PSI) was recorded. Participants (median age 30 years, IQR 26–34), 35 of whom (47.3%) developed new psychosomatic symptoms, underwent these assessments. 

Statistical analyses revealed a modest but significant reduction in pulsatility index (PI) and resistivity index (RI) in the left MCA after haze exposure in the entire cohort (PI: p = 0.026; RI: p = 0.021). However, only participants with new symptoms showed a significant decline in mean PI and RI after exposure (PI: p = 0.001; RI: p = 0.001) compared to baseline, whereas asymptomatic individuals did not (PI: p = 0.919; RI: p = 0.970). 

These findings suggest that haze exposure can cause marked cerebral vasodilation in individuals prone to psychosomatic symptoms. These hemodynamic changes may play a role in the development of such symptoms, though larger studies are needed to elucidate long-term prognostic and health impacts.

text:
Mesothelioma is a lung cancer that kills thousands of people worldwide annually, especially those with exposure to asbestos. Diagnosis of mesothelioma in patients often requires time-consuming imaging techniques and biopsies. Machine learning can provide for a more effective, cheaper, and faster patient diagnosis and feature selection from clinical data in patient records.

We analyzed a dataset of health records of 324 patients having mesothelioma symptoms from Turkey. The patients had prior asbestos exposure and displayed symptoms consistent with mesothelioma. We compared probabilistic neural network, perceptron-based neural network, random forest, one rule, and decision tree classifiers to predict diagnosis of the patient records. We measured classifiers’ performance through standard confusion matrix scores such as Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC). Random forest outperformed all models tried, obtaining MCC = +0.37 on the complete imbalanced dataset and MCC = +0.64 on the under-sampled balanced dataset. We then employed random forest feature selection to identify the two most relevant dataset traits associated with mesothelioma: lung side and platelet count. These two risk factors resulted so predictive, that decision tree focusing on them achieved the second top accuracy on the complete dataset diagnosis prediction (MCC = +0.28), outperforming all other methods and even decision tree itself applied to all features.

Our results show that machine learning can predict diagnoses of patients having mesothelioma symptoms with high accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, in few minutes. Additionally, random forest can efficiently select the most important features of this clinical dataset (lung side and platelet count) in few seconds. The importance of pleural plaques in lung sides and blood platelets in mesothelioma diagnosis indicates that physicians should focus on these two features when reading records of patients with mesothelioma symptoms. text: Anthropogenic effects have created various risks for wild animals. Boat traffic is one of the most fatal risks for marine mammals. Individual behavioral responses of cetaceans, including diving behavior such as changing swimming direction and lengthing inter-breath interval, to passing boats is relatively well known; however, the social function of cetacean responses to boat traffic in a natural setting remains poorly understood. We focused on describing the behavioral responses of single and aggregated finless porpoises to boats passing at Misumi West Port, Ariake Sound, Japan, by using a drone characterized with a high-precision bird’s-eye angle. During the study period, we collected 25 episodes of finless porpoise responses to boats passing by. A mean (± SEM) of 5.1 ± 1.0 individuals were observed for each episode. The primary response to passing boats was avoidance by dive, which implies boat traffic is a substantial disturbance to finless porpoises that travel along the seawater surface daily. The diving duration decreased significantly with an increase in the number of aggregated individuals. The diving and floating reaction times were 10.9 ± 2.3 s and 18.7 ± 5.0 s, respectively. There was no significant difference between the reaction times indicating that each individual was motivated to keep the group cohesion consistent when floating even after the risk had dissolved, which is comparable to the behavior of porpoises that dive when riskier conditions are present, such as when a boat approaches an aggregation. Our findings provide new insights on the sociality of finless porpoises even though there were limitations, like an inability to identify a specific individual. The drone enabled us to observe the social behavior of finless porpoises and other cetaceans at an unprecedented resolution, which may lead to a better understanding of the evolutionary diversity of intelligence and sociality and the bridge to human evolution.

text: Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) remains a leading cause of maternal death worldwide, and it is important to understand the relative contributions of different risk factors. We assessed the incidence of these among cases of transvaginal delivery. Between June 2013 and July 2016, a prospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary perinatal medical facility in Japan. Women were administered a questionnaire to ascertain risk factors for PPH, defined as a blood loss of 1,000 ml or more assessed using a calibrated under-buttocks drape and collection vessel at childbirth. We analyzed 1,068 transvaginal deliveries of singleton pregnancies. The incidence of PPH was 8.7%, and of severe PPH (1,500 ml blood loss or more) was 2.1%. Risk factors for postpartum hemorrhage among the deliveries were: fetal macrosomia (over 4000 g); pregnancy-induced hypertension; pregnancy generated by assisted reproductive technology; severe vaginal or perineal lacerations; and weight gain over 15 kg during pregnancy. Such high weight gain significantly increased the incidence of PPH compared with women showing less than 10 kg weight gain during pregnancy. Monitoring these identified risk factors could enable extra vigilance during labor, and preparedness for managing PPH in all women giving birth.

Etiology is unknown in approximately one-quarter of stroke patients after evaluation, which is termed cryptogenic stroke (CS). The prognosis of CS patients is largely undetermined. We created a novel index from transcranial Doppler parameters including mean flow velocity (MV) and pulsatility index (PI) and investigated whether the calculation of asymmetry in the novel parameter can predict functional outcomes in CS patients.

We made the middle cerebral artery (MCA) index (%) as a novel parameter, which was calculated as 100 X (MCA MV + MCA PI X 10) / (MCA MV–MCA PI X 10). The MCA asymmetry index (%) was also calculated as 100 X (|Rt MCA index–Lt MCA index|) / (Rt MCA index + Lt MCA index) / 2. Poor functional outcomes were defined as modified Rankin Scale score (mRS) ≥3 at 3 months after stroke onset.

A total of 377 CS patients were included. Among them, 52 (13.8%) patients had a poor outcome. The overall MCA asymmetry index was two-fold higher in CS patients with a poor outcome (10.26%) compared to those with a good outcome (5.41%, p = 0.002). In multivariable analysis, the overall MCA asymmetry index (OR, 1.054, 95% CI, 1.013–1.096, p = 0.009) and the cutoff value of the overall MCA asymmetry index >9 were associated with poor outcomes at 3 months (OR, 3.737, 95% CI, 1.530–9.128, p = 0.004).

We demonstrated that the novel asymmetric MCA index can predict short-term functional outcomes in CS patients.

text:
In this study, we investigated the predictive value of a novel asymmetric middle cerebral artery (MCA) index for functional outcomes in cryptogenic stroke (CS) patients. Etiology remains unknown in about 25% of stroke cases, termed cryptogenic stroke, with an uncertain prognosis. We calculated the MCA index using transcranial Doppler parameters: mean flow velocity (MV) and pulsatility index (PI). The MCA asymmetry index was derived from the absolute difference between right and left MCA indices, normalized by their average.

We included 377 CS patients, with 52 (13.8%) exhibiting poor functional outcomes, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score ≥3 at 3 months. The overall MCA asymmetry index was significantly higher in patients with poor outcomes (10.26%) compared to those with good outcomes (5.41%, p = 0.002). Multivariable analysis revealed that the overall MCA asymmetry index (OR, 1.054, 95% CI, 1.013–1.096, p = 0.009) and a cutoff value >9% (OR, 3.737, 95% CI, 1.530–9.128, p = 0.004) were associated with poor outcomes. Our findings indicate that the asymmetric MCA index can predict short-term functional outcomes in CS patients.

Approximately one-quarter of stroke patients, termed cryptogenic stroke (CS) patients, have an unknown etiology. The prognosis for these patients remains largely undetermined. We introduced a novel index derived from transcranial Doppler parameters—mean flow velocity (MV) and pulsatility index (PI)—to investigate whether asymmetry in this parameter could predict functional outcomes in CS patients.

Additionally, we calculated the MCA asymmetry index (%) as follows: 100 × (|Rt MCA index – Lt MCA index|) / ((Rt MCA index + Lt MCA index) / 2). Poor functional outcomes were defined as a modified Rankin Scale score (mRS) ≥3 at three months post-stroke onset.

Our study included 377 CS patients, of which 52 (13.8%) exhibited poor outcomes. The overall MCA asymmetry index was significantly higher in patients with poor outcomes (10.26%) compared to those with good outcomes (5.41%, p = 0.002). Multivariable analysis revealed that the overall MCA asymmetry index (OR, 1.054, 95% CI, 1.013–1.096, p = 0.009) and a cutoff value exceeding 9% were associated with poor outcomes at three months (OR, 3.737, 95% CI, 1.530–9.128, p = 0.004).

Our findings demonstrate that the novel asymmetric MCA index can effectively predict short-term functional outcomes in CS patients.

text: Evidence shows that selective attention to visual stimuli modulates the gain of cochlear responses, probably through auditory-cortex descending pathways. At the cerebral cortex level, amplitude and phase changes of neural oscillations have been proposed as a correlate of selective attention. However, whether sensory receptors are also influenced by the oscillatory network during attention tasks remains unknown. Here, we searched for oscillatory attention-related activity at the cochlear receptor level in humans. We used an alternating visual/auditory selective attention task and measured electroencephalographic activity simultaneously to distortion product otoacoustic emissions (a measure of cochlear receptor-cell activity). In order to search for cochlear oscillatory activity, the otoacoustic emission signal, was included as an additional channel in the electroencephalogram analyses. This method allowed us to evaluate dynamic changes in cochlear oscillations within the same range of frequencies (1–35 Hz) in which cognitive effects are commonly observed in electroencephalogram works. We found the presence of low frequency (<10 Hz) brain and cochlear amplifier oscillations during selective attention to visual and auditory stimuli. Notably, switching between auditory and visual attention modulates the amplitude and the temporal order of brain and inner ear oscillations. These results extend the role of the oscillatory activity network during cognition in neural systems to the receptor level.

text: Selective attention to visual stimuli modulates cochlear response gain, likely via auditory-cortex descending pathways. At the cortical level, amplitude and phase changes in neural oscillations correlate with selective attention. However, the influence of oscillatory networks on sensory receptors during attention tasks is unknown. This study investigated oscillatory attention-related activity at the cochlear receptor level in humans. These findings suggest that oscillatory activity during cognition extends to the receptor level, implicating cochlear oscillations in attentional processes.

This aggregation may facilitate their uptake by larger zooplankton, thereby providing an alternative trophic pathway that short-circuits conventional food webs and influences higher trophic levels. text:
Magic roundabout (ROBO4) is an unusual endothelial-specific paralog of the family of neuronally-expressed axon guidance receptors called roundabouts. Endothelial cells (ECs), whose uninterrupted sheet delimits the lumen of all vertebrate blood vessels and which are absent from invertebrate species, are a vertebrate-specific evolutionary novelty.

Herein, the evolutionary mechanism of the duplication, retention and divergence of ROBO4 was investigated for the first time. Phylogenetic analyses carried out suggested that ROBO4 is a fast-evolving paralog of ROBO1 formed at the base of vertebrates. The ancestral expression pattern was neuronal. ROBO4 dramatically shifted its expression and became exceptionally specific to ECs. The data-mining of FANTOM5 and ENCODE reveals that ROBO4’s endothelial expression arises from a single transcription start site (TSS), conserved in mouse, controlled by a proximal promoter with a complex architecture suggestive of regulatory neo-functionalization. (An analysis of promoter probabilities suggested the architecture was not due to a chance arrangement of TFBSes). Further evidence for the neo-functionalization of ROBO4 comes from the analysis of its protein interactions, the rates of protein evolution, and of positively selected sites.

The neo-functionalization model explains why ROBO4 protein acquired new context-specific biological functions in the control of angiogenesis. This endothelial-specific roundabout receptor is an illustrative example of the emergence of an essential vertebrate molecular novelty and an endothelial-specific signaling sub-network through 2R-WGD. The emergence of novel cell types, such as ECs, might be a neglected evolutionary force contributing to the high rate of retention of duplicates post-2R-WGD. Crucially, expression neo-functionalization to evolutionarily novel sites of expression conceptually extends the classical model of neo-functionalization.

text: Magic roundabout (ROBO4) is an endothelial-specific paralog of the neuronally expressed roundabout (ROBO) family of axon guidance receptors. Unlike invertebrates, vertebrates possess endothelial cells (ECs)—a cell type defining the inner lining of blood vessels and absent in invertebrate lineages—representing a vertebrate-specific evolutionary innovation. This study presents the first investigation into the evolutionary mechanism behind the duplication, retention, and functional divergence of ROBO4. Phylogenetic analyses indicate ROBO4 arose as a fast-evolving paralog of ROBO1 at the base of the vertebrate lineage. While its ancestral expression was neuronal, ROBO4 underwent a dramatic shift to become highly specific to endothelial cells. Data mining of FANTOM5 and ENCODE databases shows ROBO4’s endothelial expression is driven by a single, conserved transcription start site (TSS) in both human and mouse, regulated by a proximal promoter with complex architecture. The likelihood that this promoter structure arose by chance is low, as supported by an analysis of transcription factor binding site (TFBS) probabilities, suggesting functional significance. Additional evidence for neo-functionalization comes from ROBO4’s distinct protein interaction profile, elevated rates of protein evolution, and the presence of positively selected sites. These findings collectively support a model in which ROBO4 acquired new, context-specific roles in regulating angiogenesis. As a vertebrate-specific receptor with a specialized role in endothelial signaling, ROBO4 exemplifies how 2R-WGD (two rounds of whole-genome duplication) contributed to the emergence of essential molecular novelties. The evolution of novel cell types like ECs may have played a previously underappreciated role in the high retention of gene duplicates after 2R-WGD. Importantly, the acquisition of expression in an evolutionarily novel cell type—endothelial cells—extends the classical definition of neo-functionalization to include expression site shifts, highlighting a broader mechanism for functional innovation in gene families.

text: Hepatic fibrosis develops from a series of complex interactions among resident and recruited cells making it a challenge to replicate using standard in vitro approaches. While studies have demonstrated the importance of macrophages in fibrogenesis, the role of Kupffer cells (KCs) in modulating the initial response remains elusive. Previous work demonstrated utility of 3D bioprinted liver to recapitulate basic fibrogenic features following treatment with fibrosis-associated agents. In the present study, culture conditions were modified to recapitulate a gradual accumulation of collagen within the tissues over an extended exposure timeframe. Under these conditions, KCs were added to the model to examine their impact on the injury/fibrogenic response following cytokine and drug stimuli. A 28-day exposure to 10 ng/mL TGF-β1 and 0.209 μM methotrexate (MTX) resulted in sustained LDH release which was attenuated when KCs were incorporated in the model. Assessment of miR-122 confirmed early hepatocyte injury in response to TGF-β1 that appeared delayed in the presence of KCs, whereas MTX-induced increases in miR-122 were observed when KCs were incorporated in the model. Although the collagen responses were mild under the conditions tested to mimic early fibrotic injury, a global reduction in cytokines was observed in the KC-modified tissue model following treatment. Furthermore, gene expression profiling suggests KCs have a significant impact on baseline tissue function over time and an important modulatory role dependent on the context of injury. Although the number of differentially expressed genes across treatments was comparable, pathway enrichment suggests distinct, KC- and time-dependent changes in the transcriptome for each agent. As such, the incorporation of KCs and impact on baseline tissue homeostasis may be important in recapitulating temporal dynamics of the fibrogenic response to different agents.

text: Hepatic fibrosis arises from intricate crosstalk between resident and recruited cells, presenting challenges for accurate in vitro modeling. While macrophages are known to contribute to fibrogenesis, the specific role of Kupffer cells (KCs) in shaping the early injury and fibrotic response remains unclear. Building on prior work showing that 3D bioprinted liver models can reproduce core fibrogenic features upon exposure to fibrosis-inducing agents, this study refined culture conditions to support a gradual, sustained accumulation of collagen over a 28-day period. KCs were introduced into the system to evaluate their influence on the response to cytokine and drug stimuli. Exposure to 10 ng/mL TGF-β1 and 0.209 μM methotrexate (MTX) led to prolonged LDH release, a marker of membrane damage, which was reduced when KCs were present. miR-122 levels, used as an indicator of hepatocyte injury, rose early in response to TGF-β1, but this increase was delayed in KC-containing cultures. Although collagen deposition was modest under these conditions—reflecting an early injury phase—overall cytokine release was lower in KC-modified models following treatment. Gene expression analysis revealed that KCs significantly shape baseline tissue function over time, and their impact is context-dependent. While the total number of differentially expressed genes was similar across treatments, pathway enrichment highlighted distinct, KC- and time-dependent transcriptomic shifts for each agent. These findings suggest that KCs not only modulate the response to specific insults but also alter baseline tissue homeostasis, influencing the temporal dynamics of fibrogenesis. The inclusion of KCs thus appears critical for accurately capturing the evolution of the fibrogenic response in engineered liver models.

text:
Human Immunodeficiency Virus infection (HIV) remains a public health concern in Cameroon that requires regular surveillance for informed policy-making to guide programmatic interventions. Using data from the 2016 HIV national sentinel survey in Cameroon, we ascertained HIV prevalence and factors associated with risk of infection among pregnant women

A cross-sectional study was conducted throughout 2016 in the 10 regions of Cameroon, targeting 7000 first antenatal care (ANC-1) attendees (4000 from urban and 3000 from rural areas) in 60 sentinel health facilities. HIV serological test was performed using the national serial algorithm at the National Reference Laboratory (NRL). Prevalence was determined, and multivariate logistic regression was used to assess determinants of HIV infection, with p-value<0.05 considered statistically significant.

Of the 7000 targeted participants, a total of 6859 first ANC-1 attendees were enrolled (98.0% sampling coverage). Median age was 26 [IQR: 21–30] years and 47,40% had a secondary school level of education. The national prevalence of HIV was 5.70% (95% CI: 4.93–6.40) and range from 9.7% in East region to 2.6% in North region. The prevalence was 5.58% (95% CI: 95%: 4.88–6.35) in urban and 5.87% (95% CI: 5.04–6.78) in rural settings. Factors that were associated with HIV infection included marital status, women who were married or living with their partner are less likely to be infected than singles women (aOR = 0.60; 95% CI: 0.46–0.78), multiparity [aOR = 1.5(95%CI:1.0–2.2)] and been living in the Centre, East, North-west and South-west regions. HIV infection was also significantly associated with age, with the risk of being infected increasing with age.

Pregnant women in Cameroon are still disproportionately infected with HIV compared with the general population (prevalence 4.3%). Preventive actions to curb the epidemic amongst pregnant women should prioritize interventions targeting single pregnant women, who are older, and residing particularly in the Centre, East, North West and South West regions of the country.

A cross-sectional study conducted across Cameroon’s 10 regions in 2016 evaluated HIV prevalence and associated risk factors among first antenatal care attendees. Targeted interventions should focus on single pregnant women, particularly those older than 25 and residing in the Centre, East, North-West, and South-West regions. These findings underscore the need for risk-stratified prevention strategies to address disparities and reduce vertical transmission.

text:
Human Immunodeficiency Virus infection (HIV) remains a public health challenge in Cameroon, necessitating ongoing surveillance to inform policy and guide interventions. Data from the 2016 national HIV sentinel survey were used to assess HIV prevalence and associated risk factors among pregnant women attending first antenatal care (ANC-1). A cross-sectional study was conducted across all 10 regions of Cameroon in 60 sentinel health facilities, with 7000 first ANC-1 attendees targeted—4000 from urban and 3000 from rural areas. HIV serological testing followed the national serial algorithm at the National Reference Laboratory. Prevalence was calculated, and multivariate logistic regression identified determinants of infection, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant.

Of the 7000 targeted individuals, 6859 were enrolled, representing 98.0% sampling coverage. The median age was 26 years (IQR: 21–30), and 47.4% had secondary school education. The national HIV prevalence was 5.70% (95% CI: 4.93–6.40), ranging from 2.6% in the North to 9.7% in the East. Prevalence was 5.58% (95% CI: 4.88–6.35) in urban areas and 5.87% (95% CI: 5.04–6.78) in rural areas. Factors independently associated with HIV infection included marital status: women who were married or cohabiting had lower odds of infection compared to single women (aOR = 0.60; 95% CI: 0.46–0.78). Multiparity was also associated with higher risk (aOR = 1.5; 95% CI: 1.0–2.2). Residence in the Centre, East, North-West, and South-West regions was linked to increased HIV prevalence. Age was positively associated with infection risk, with prevalence rising with advancing age.

HIV prevalence among pregnant women in Cameroon (5.70%) exceeds that in the general population (4.3%). Preventive strategies should focus on single pregnant women, who are older and concentrated in the Centre, East, North-West, and South-West regions. Targeted interventions in these populations and settings are required to reduce transmission and support prevention of mother-to-child transmission.

text:
British footballer David Beckham has arrived in Trinidad and Tobago amid fears of kidnapping. Beckham travelled to the island of Trinidad to watch the final of the FIFA women's Under 17s World Cup final and to launch a football festival for children. The stars arrival is also speculated to help England's bid for the 2018 World Cup.

Beckham's safety has come into question while he is visiting the island. Trinidad and Tobago have one of the highest murder and kidnap rates in the world. Beckham, who is reported to have a 125m fortune, could be a high target for a ransom kidnap. Upon his arrival, there were a numerous amount of police on scene as well as Beckham's own personal security team.

Along with FIFA president Sepp Blatter, Beckham watched the women's Under 17s World Cup final which saw South Korea defeat Japan to win the cup. The football festival he will host on Monday has gained criticism from officals. The host of the festival is the Marvin Lee Stadium; Lee was the captain of the Trinidad and Tobago national football team and died during a match in 2003 when he collided with Landon Donovan, a current teammate of Beckham.

The death toll from the weekend suspension bridge collapse on the Indonesian island of Borneo has risen from four to eleven. Search and rescue teams continue to look for bodies in the Mahakam River.

Cars, motorbikes, and buses all fell into the Mahakam River when the bridge came down during repairs. Another car was left overturned and balanced upon wreckage over the water. State-owned builders PT Hutama Karya completed the bridge about a decade ago in the image of California's Golden Gate Bridge. A cable on the 720-metre structure is thought to have failed as workers dealt with it; six of the repair crew were reported missing yesterday. It had been the longest suspension bridge in Borneo.

National search and rescue head Daryatmo said yesterday cranes will attempt to move debris today, with new reports saying echo-sounding equipment will be used to check it is safe to begin lifting. It is believed the bodies of more victims will be found trapped in vehicles beneath the water, which is 35-40 metres deep. Visibility is poor, and one official explained authorities are still unsure how many vehicles are on the riverbed.

Samarinda's seen a population and construction boom lately. A few years have seen the population triple and the construction of a large mosque, and a sports stadium; an airport and port are set to follow. However, the Corruption Eradication Commission warns 70% of the corruption it investigates concerns government contracts and up to 40% of money earmarked for infrastructure ends up stolen.

Its population has tripled, and new construction includes a large mosque, a sports stadium, and upcoming plans for an airport and port. The sub-body, called the Subsidiary Body for Implementation (SBI) is, as its name implies, amongst other things responsible for preparing and implementing decisions of the main body of the UNFCCC, the Conference of the Parties (COP). After having spent a large part of the morning discussing formalities regarding whether or not technology transfer was to be taken up as a separate item, the afternoon session had to be extended till around 9 pm local time. Even then some of the planned agenda items had not been concluded when the session closed.

The cause for discussion in the morning were two different interpretations of a decision the COP made yesterday: Member states of the G77+C believed that the referral of the item of tech transfer by the COP automatically lead to its inclusion on the agenda as a separate item, while the Chairman of the SBI and the US voiced the opinion that to for it to be included, the item would have to be formally agreed upon in the normal manner. Compromise, of one sort or another, could not be reached, and it was only after a legal adviser stated that in his point of view the item indeed was necessarily included on the agenda as a separate item that the matter could be concluded.

Due to the stalling in the mornings session, discussions on the actual item of technology transfer began after what would have been the scheduled closing time. South Africa made the proposal to set up a contact group for the item, so that it could be discussed in a setting with less participants in an informal way. A number of G77+C nations (including China and Nigeria) spoke out in support of this proposal, emphasizing that rapid progress was needed on the issue. Japan, and the US made critical statements, noting that they believed that the scope of the contact group should first be established, and that it would be more sensible to establish the contact group in 2008. After it was found that the group would nevertheless be established, the Chairman asked for suggestions for Co-chairs of the group, as one from the Annex I and one from the non Annex one would be required. The non-Annex I having already decided that they supported Prof. Philip M. Gwage from Uganda as Co-chair, the Annex I countries decided that Jukka Uosukainen from Finland would be the Co-chair on their behalf after brief deliberations. The decision being reached provoked some applause from delegates and observers, and the session was closed shortly thereafter.

The subsidiary body responsible for implementing decisions within the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), known as the Subsidiary Body for Implementation (SBI), faced a lengthy discussion over the inclusion of technology transfer as a separate agenda item. The morning session was largely consumed by this debate, leading to an extended afternoon session that concluded around 9 pm local time. Despite this, some planned agenda items remained unresolved when the session closed.

The morning's discussion stemmed from two differing interpretations of a recent Conference of the Parties (COP) decision. The G77+Ch group of countries believed that the COP's referral of the technology transfer item automatically included it as a separate agenda item. However, the SBI Chairman and the United States argued that formal agreement was necessary for its inclusion. A compromise could not be reached until a legal adviser clarified that the item was indeed automatically included as a separate agenda item.

Due to the morning's delay, discussions on the technology transfer item began after the scheduled closing time. South Africa proposed establishing a contact group to discuss the item informally with fewer participants. Several G77+C nations, including China and Nigeria, supported this proposal, stressing the need for rapid progress. However, Japan and the US expressed concerns, suggesting that the scope of the contact group should be established first and that its formation should occur in 2008.

Despite these objections, the contact group was formed. The Chairman requested suggestions for Co-chairs, one from the Annex I group of developed countries and one from the non-Annex I group. The non-Annex I countries had already decided to support Prof. Philip M. Gwage from Uganda as Co-chair. After brief deliberations, the Annex I countries chose Jukka Uosukainen from Finland to serve as their Co-chair. This decision was met with applause from delegates and observers, and the session was subsequently closed.

text: Hibbert, an imprisoned innocent, is caught up in the jailbreak of his cellmate Scarlatti, engineered with the assistance of another man, Burks. Forcing Hibbert to accompany them, Scarlatti and Burks make for the Florida Everglades, picking up Scarlatti's girlfriend Carlotta on the way. In the Everglades the four encounter a miraculous golden stairway extending into the sky. Ascending, they find a pool defended by a blue flamingo, which is killed by Burks. Another stairway leads them to the land of Khoire, a strange and mysterious paradise. There a man named Patur exposes the true nature of each by means of a crystal mask. He warns them that they will be transformed in accordance with those natures within a day, and must leave Khoire. Scarlatti and Carlotta's alteration is horrible, and they are consumed by a huge beast; Burks agrees to become a blue flamingo, taking the place of the guardian of the pool, in the hope of some day being readmitted to Khoire. Hibbert is little changed. Returning to the mundane world, he undertakes to find certain persons who can help him gain his own readmittance to Khoire, having fallen in love with one of its denizens, Mareth of the Watchers.

text:
A Dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN) is a Bayesian network (BN) which relates variables to each other over adjacent time steps. This is often called a Two-Timeslice BN (2TBN) because it says that at any point in time T, the value of a variable can be calculated from the internal regressors and the immediate prior value (time T-1).  DBNs were developed by Paul Dagum in the early 1990s at Stanford University's Section on Medical Informatics. Dagum developed DBNs to unify and extend traditional linear state-space models such as Kalman filters, linear and normal forecasting models such as ARMA and simple dependency models such as hidden Markov models into a general probabilistic representation and inference mechanism for arbitrary nonlinear and non-normal time-dependent domains.
Today, DBNs are common in robotics, and have shown potential for a wide range of data mining applications.  For example, they have been used in speech recognition, digital forensics, protein sequencing, and bioinformatics.  DBN is a generalization of hidden Markov models and Kalman filters.
DBNs are conceptually related to Probabilistic Boolean Networks  and can, similarly, be used to model dynamical systems at steady-state.

text:
Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs) connect variables across successive points in time by relating each variable’s state to its own past values and internal causes at the previous step—a structure often called a two-timeslice network. Originating in the early 1990s, they were created by Paul Dagum at Stanford’s Section on Medical Informatics. Dagum designed DBNs to bring together different modeling approaches like linear state-space models (such as Kalman filters), ARMA models, and hidden Markov models into one flexible probabilistic framework suitable even for complex, non-linear, and non-Gaussian systems.

Modern applications of DBNs include fields like robotics, where they help with tasks involving uncertainty and temporal reasoning. The technique has also been applied in areas such as speech recognition, digital forensics, protein sequencing, and bioinformatics. DBNs extend hidden Markov models and Kalman filters, offering broader modeling capabilities. They are also conceptually linked to Probabilistic Boolean Networks and can be adapted to describe steady-state systems as well.

DBNs are conceptually related to Probabilistic Boolean Networks  and can, similarly, be used to model dynamical systems at steady-state.

text:
Visual perception is the ability to interpret the surrounding environment through photopic vision (daytime vision), color vision, scotopic vision (night vision), and mesopic vision (twilight vision), using light in the visible spectrum reflected by objects in the environment. This is different from visual acuity, which refers to how clearly a person sees (for example "20/20 vision"). A person can have problems with visual perceptual processing even if they have 20/20 vision.
The resulting perception is also known as vision, sight, or eyesight (adjectives visual, optical, and ocular, respectively). The various physiological components involved in vision are referred to collectively as the visual system, and are the focus of much research in linguistics, psychology, cognitive science, neuroscience, and molecular biology, collectively referred to as vision science.

text: People see their surroundings thanks to several processes that fall under visual perception. This includes interpreting daytime sight (photopic vision), recognizing colors (color vision), and seeing in low or dim light (scotopic and mesopic vision), all because light in the visible spectrum bounces off objects and enters the eyes. Visual acuity, such as "20/20 vision," measures how clearly someone can see at a distance, but it doesn't capture the whole story; many people can have good acuity yet still struggle to process visual information. Together, all the physical and neurological mechanisms involved in seeing are called the visual system, which scientists study across many fields to understand how vision actually works.

text: The story is about a boy named Beric, who is raised amongst the Dumnonii. After coming of age, his status within their culture comes under pressure, shown in a conflict between the acceptance of the village Bard and the condemnation on religious grounds by the village Druid. After a bad harvest is linked to his presence, the superstitious views of the Druid win-out, and Beric is exiled from the tribe. He journeys to Isca Dumnoniorum, where he falls afoul of a Greek slave trader, who tricks Beric and takes him as a slave. He us ultimately purchased by Publius Pio, a Roman Magistrate, and becomes part of Pio's patrician household on the Viminal Hill. Beric antagonizes Glaucus, son of Publius Pio, embarrassing Glaucus at a dinner celebrating Pio's election to the office of Aedile. This scene is witnessed by Centurion Justinius, and results in Beric being condemned to work in the salt mines, a certain slow and painful death. Beric makes his escape from Pio's household, hiding in a disused temple of Sylvan Pan, and making his way north on the Via Flaminia, hoping to walk back to Britain. He is caught in the Roman countryside, condemned as a bandit, and sentenced to live out his life as a galley slave. He works in the Rhenus Fleet, stationed in Colonia Agrippina, living many years on the galley 'Alcestis'. His galley is eventually sent to Britain, surviving a great storm, during which Beric is thrown overboard for dead. Beric washes ashore for the second time in his life, this time to be rescued by the Roman British household of the centurion Justinius, who had returned to his duty station after his leave in Rome. Beric now joins in the work on the Rhee Wall of Romney Marsh, where the Romans led by Justinius are working reclaim land from the sea. Richard Kennedy's cover art is in color, while the illustrations within the novel are black and white charcoal drawings.

text:
Beric grew up among the Dumnonii, a boy shaped by the dense forests and close-knit customs of his people. As he reached adulthood, the important question of his status within the tribe came to a head. The village Bard quietly supported his place in the community, but the stern Druid, deeply influenced by ancient superstitions, spoke against Beric, blaming a poor harvest on his very presence. In the end, superstition carried more weight than reason, and Beric found himself banished from the tribe. 

Seeking refuge, he made his way south to Isca, a city thick with foreign scents and sharper tongues. There, a cunning Greek slave dealer saw opportunity in Beric’s youth and naiveté, tricking the boy into being taken as a captive. Eventually, Beric’s fortunes changed when a Roman official, Publius Pio, bought him and brought him into his home on the Viminal Hill. Yet, even in the comfort of this new world, Beric could not escape friction. He provoked Glaucus, the ambitious younger son of Pio, at a celebratory feast marking Pio’s new magistracy. The incident, witnessed by the stern Centurion Justinius, sealed Beric’s fate—he was sentenced to labor in the brutal salt mines.

Desperate to escape, Beric slipped away under cover of night, seeking shelter in an abandoned temple devoted to the wild god Sylvan Pan. There, he rested until the road north called him again, traveling along the Via Flaminia. His journey was marred by suspicion; misjudged as a bandit in Roman territory, he was thrown into the galleys of the Rhenus Fleet near Colonia Agrippina. Years passed as Beric toiled beneath the sun and rain aboard the ship Alcestis, the very name recalling old Greek tragedies. The ship was eventually bound for Britain, battered by a fierce storm at sea. Beric, presumed dead, washed ashore once more, only to be discovered by the household of Justinius, the centurion who had once seen him in Rome. Drawn by fate or mercy, Justinius returned Beric to the frontier, where the Romans were building the Rhee Wall against the restless sea in Romney Marsh.

There, working alongside soldiers and local laborers, Beric found himself tested again—not just by the land, but by the people. In the chaos of the great storm that followed, Beric formed a bond with his fellow workers. For the first time, he felt at home—not because he was accepted by all, but because he no longer felt wholly outcast. The journey of his soul mirrored the journey of his body: from the forests of Dumnonia, to the slavers of Greece, the salt mines of theRomans, and finally to the muddy banks of the Rhee Wall. Like in many tales by Sutcliff, the story of Beric is one of constant longing for belonging, complicated by the shifting thresholds of suspicion, pride, and unexpected kinship. In the end, Beric’s fate was intertwined with the very wall that separated the known from the unknown—a barrier both of sand and of society. And as the winds changed and the wall rose higher, Beric’s sense of place began at last to settle, shaped by the people and the land he had survived.

text:
Beric, a boy raised among the Dumnonii, faces a crisis of belonging as he comes of age. Tension arises when his status is questioned—supported by the village Bard, but rejected on religious grounds by the village Druid. The arrival of a poor harvest intensifies superstitious fears, and the Druids' suspicions prevail. Condemned by the tribe, Beric is exiled and sets out for Isca Dumnoniorum. There, a Greek slave trader deceives him, taking him as a slave before eventually selling Beric to Roman Magistrate Publius Pio. 

In Pio’s household on the Viminal Hill, Beric’s presence irritates Glaucus, Publius Pio’s son. At a celebratory dinner for Pio’s recent election as Aedile, Beric inadvertently embarrasses Glaucus, an incident observed by Centurion Justinius. As a result, Beric is sentenced to hard labor in the salt mines—a slow, painful fate that he narrowly escapes by fleeing Pio’s home and seeking shelter in the ruins of a temple dedicated to Sylvan Pan. Beric continues north on the Via Flaminia, hoping to return to Britain, but he is caught in the Roman countryside. Accused of banditry and sentenced as a galley slave, he spends years toiling on the galleys of the Rhenus Fleet anchored at Colonia Agrippina. 

His ordeal reaches a turning point when the galleys, including his ship the ‘Alcestis’, are caught in a violent storm off Britain. The tempest is so fierce that Beric is thrown overboard and believed dead. To his astonishment, he washes ashore a second time, this time discovered by Justinius’s household, now based again in Britain. Moved to the defensive works of the Rhee Wall in Romney Marsh, Beric joins Justinius’s Roman forces as they fight to reclaim land from the sea. Here, amid the labor and peril of building the wall, Beric finds a sense of belonging. His journey—from exile and alienation through various societies—culminates in acceptance, symbolized by his growing bond with a mixed-breed dog that, after birth, allows its pup to fall at his feet. Like many of Sutcliff’s novels, Outcast explores the pain and hope of the outcast, while its black-and-white charcoal illustrations and Kennedy’s colored cover bring its ancient world to life.

In Sorrow, Shen Fu points out that most of his life frustrations are out of his uprightness and his commitment to words. Though this chapter opens with the author’s own sorrow, actually its large content deals with the bumpy life of Chen Yun which is also due her characters. The content is full of the author’s endless love for his wife and resentment to the unfaire fate. The Joys of Travel not only portrays beautiful scenic spots the author had visited but also records anecdotes, local customs and historical allusions. Different from others, the author holds the belif that the gaining of experience counts rather than having a rough view and following what others said.

text:
Shen Fu's writings, collectively known as Wedded Bliss, center on his love for his wife, Chen Yun. She was not conventionally beautiful but pursued elegance naturally. Chen Yun's interests included painting, embroidery, and poetry, and she valued a simple life. Shen Fu viewed her as a close friend, sharing his hobbies and emotions. However, this perspective was not accepted by the traditional society, leaving Shen Fu's appreciation for beauty as a personal yearning.

In Little Pleasures of Life, Shen Fu recounts leisure activities from his childhood and adulthood. As a child, he found joy in nature, but as an adult, his time for such pursuits diminished due to worldly responsibilities. Many episodes describe aesthetic experiences worth contemplating. In Sorrow, Shen Fu attributes his life's frustrations to his integrity and dedication to literature. The chapter also details Chen Yun's struggles, stemming from her character. It reflects Shen Fu's profound love for his wife and resentment towards their harsh fate.

The Joys of Travel documents Shen Fu's journeys, describing scenic spots, anecdotes, local customs, and historical references. Unlike others, Shen Fu believed in gaining personal experiences rather than relying on others' views or superficial impressions. His works offer a blend of personal introspection and vivid descriptions, providing insights into his life, relationships, and philosophical beliefs.

text: Kelvin, freed from his strict Calvinist upbringing through discovering Nietzsche and 'the divine Ingersoll' in the library of his home town of Glaik, travels to swinging-sixties London to succeed as a television interviewer and newspaper columnist through nothing more than his aptitude for spin and a diabolical will to power, only to return, chastened, to Scotland and to God. Drawing on a mixture of Scottish archetypes and British stereotypes and expressing all the author's cynicism towards religion, the media and the imperial British centre, this brief fable was reportedly inspired by Gray's own visit to London as a struggling artist to record a documentary called Under The Helmet (in which he tried to increase his sales by suggesting that he was dead).

text: After escaping the rigid discipline of his Calvinist upbringing—fueled by Nietzsche and a memorable encounter with the writings of Ingersoll in his hometown’s library—Kelvin set sail for roaring London of the 1960s. Armed only with sharp wit and a ruthless determination to shape narratives, he quickly rose as a television interviewer and sharp-tongued newspaper columnist. Yet, the relentless chase for influence left him hollow. Eventually, worn by cynicism and the failures he faced at the heart of British power, Kelvin returned to Scotland. There, reflection led him back toward a sense of God, offering him a quieter, perhaps truer kind of strength. This brief tale, inspired by Gray’s own foray into London as a struggling artist and the making of his documentary “Under The Helmet,” tells the story of ambition’s double edge.

text: Exploratory data analysis (EDA) is a way of looking at data to understand its key features, mostly through charts, graphs, and visual tools. It’s not about confirming a pre-set idea—instead, it’s about letting the data speak, which sets it apart from traditional hypothesis testing. John Tukey pushed this approach starting in the 1970s, urging statisticians to dig into data without rigid models first, so they might spot patterns, spot outliers, or come up with new questions that could guide future studies. EDA isn’t just about making pretty pictures; it’s a serious method to explore what the data shows beyond formal models. It’s different from initial data analysis (IDA), which is more about fixing data—handling missing values, checking assumptions, and transforming variables—before running formal tests. EDA includes all of IDA, but goes further by focusing on discovery, not just preparation.

text:
Face ID is a facial recognition system designed and developed by Apple Inc. for the iPhone and iPad Pro. The system allows biometric authentication for unlocking a device, making payments, accessing sensitive data, providing detailed facial expression tracking for Animoji, as well as six degrees of freedom (6DOF) head-tracking, eye-tracking, and other features. Initially released in November 2017 with the iPhone X, it has since been updated and introduced to several new iPhone models, and all iPad Pro models.
The Face ID hardware consists of a sensor with three modules; a dot projector that projects a grid of small infrared dots onto a user's face, a module called the flood illuminator that shines infrared light at the face, and an infrared camera which takes an infrared picture of the user, reads the resulting pattern and generates a 3D facial map. This map is compared with the registered face using a secure subsystem, and the user is authenticated if the two faces match sufficiently. The system can recognize faces with glasses, clothing, makeup, and facial hair, and adapts to changes in appearance over time.
Face ID has sparked a number of debates about security and privacy. Apple claims that Face ID is statistically more advanced than Touch ID fingerprint scanning. It exhibits significantly fewer false positives. Still, Face ID has shown issues at separating identical twins. Multiple security features largely limit the risk of the system being bypassed using photos or masks, and only one proof-of-concept attempt using detailed scans has succeeded. Debate continues over the lack of legal protections offered by biometric systems as compared to passcode authentication in the United States. Privacy advocates have also expressed concern about third-party app developers' access to "rough maps" of user facial data, despite rigid requirements by Apple of how developers handle facial data.
On some devices, Face ID is unable to recognize users wearing face masks. Apple responded to criticism by offering faster fallback to passcode input, and the option for Apple Watch users to confirm whether they intended to unlock their iPhone. In March 2022, Apple released iOS 15.4 which adds mask-compatible Face ID for iPhone 12 and later devices.

text:
Face ID is Apple’s facial recognition system, built into the iPhone and all iPad Pro models. It’s used to unlock devices, authorize payments, access secure data, power Animoji with detailed facial expression tracking, and enable 6DOF head and eye tracking. First launched in November 2017 with the iPhone X, it’s since been integrated into newer iPhone models and all iPad Pro variants.

The system relies on three components in a dedicated sensor: a dot projector that bathes the face in a pattern of infrared dots, a flood illuminator that emits infrared light to help capture the face in low light, and an infrared camera that reads the distorted pattern of dots and builds a 3D facial map. This map is compared against the registered facial data using a secure subsystem, and authentication occurs if the match meets a set threshold. The system works with glasses, makeup, facial hair, and clothing, and it adapts over time to natural changes in a user’s appearance.

Apple says Face ID is statistically more secure than Touch ID, with far fewer false positives. However, it can’t reliably distinguish between identical twins. While multiple security measures prevent most spoofing attempts—like using photos or masks—only one proof-of-concept using high-resolution 3D scans has successfully bypassed it. Concerns remain over the lack of legal protections for biometric data in the U.S. compared to passcodes. Privacy advocates have also questioned how third-party apps access rough facial maps, though Apple enforces strict guidelines on how developers may use that data.

In response to pandemic-related mask use, Face ID initially failed on users wearing face coverings. Apple addressed this by speeding up the fallback to passcode entry and enabling Apple Watch to confirm unlock intent. In March 2022, iOS 15.4 introduced mask-compatible Face ID for iPhone 12 and later models, allowing users to unlock their devices while wearing masks, as long as the eyes and nose are visible.

The rest of the plot follows how the boys help capture the crooks and eventually, how the lost ruby is found.

text: Frank and Joe Hardy arrive at Alfred McVay’s Arizona ranch to find him shaken, having just been attacked by the infamous jewel thief Oscar Tamm. McVay, a passionate collector, reveals he’s been plagued by odd occurrences—strange footprints, locked doors, and a sense of being watched. He hires the brothers to protect him, unaware they’re already deep in a web of deception. The foreman, Wat Perkins, strikes them as unnaturally stiff and evasive. The butler, Wilbur, moves with quiet precision, but his eyes linger too long on the locked display case. A shadowy rider appears at night, vanishing before dawn—sending signals, it seems, to someone inside. Then the storm hits: a sudden, violent tornado tears through the property. In the chaos, the Crimson Flame, a blood-red ruby famed for its fire-like gleam, vanishes. McVay withdraws into silence. Armed with a torn note, a smudged horse track, and a photograph hidden behind a wall panel, the Hardys follow the trail across continents, into Thailand. There, they piece together the thieves’ network, confront the mastermind, and recover the stone—its brilliance restored, not by law, but by the brothers’ relentless eye for what no one else saw.

text: Sorcerer Cray Ormoru and his friend, the seer Feldar Sepwin, craft an enchanted mirror that allows whoever gazes upon it to see their heart's desire. For Cray himself, the mirror remains blank for many years, until one day he sees in it the image of a young girl. With no idea of who she is, he watches the girl transform into a lovely woman over the years, and Cray realizes that he is destined to find her. When he does, he learns that this is Aliza, a sorceress who lives in a crystal palace which is partly within the demon realm and who is dedicated solely to the study of her craft. Cray finds Aliza to be a skilled young sorceress, but also cold, aloof, and entirely focused on sorcery. Cray encourages her to take an interest in the outside world and forms a budding friendship. However, this friendship is strongly discouraged by Aliza's sorcerer grandfather, Everand. Despite Everand's disapproval, Aliza and Cray travel to the demon realm and also to the home of Cray's sorceress mother, Delivev. During this latter journey, Aliza looks into the mirror of heart's desire and causes it to shatter. This causes some initial confusion, but it is quickly revealed this is because Aliza's soul has been stolen from her. Ultimately, her grandfather Everand is shown to be a villain of the worst degree. He uses Aliza's soul and his capture of Feldar as leverage to demand Aliza and Cray's obedience. However, Cray rallies his allies from the demon realm in order to confront and defeat Everand and free Aliza's soul. With her soul freed, Cray and Aliza realize their love for each other.

Sorcerer Cray Ormoru and his friend, the seer Feldar Sepwin, created an enchanted mirror that revealed each viewer's heart's desire. For Cray, the mirror remained empty for many years until he glimpsed a young girl within it. Over time, he watched her grow into a beautiful woman, sensing that he was meant to find her. Despite Everand's opposition, Aliza and Cray journeyed to the demon realm and to Cray's mother Delivev's home. During this trip, Aliza gazed into the heart's desire mirror, causing it to shatter. The destruction revealed that Aliza's soul had been stolen. Everand was the culprit, using Aliza's soul and Feldar's capture to coerce Cray and Aliza into obedience. Cray rallied allies from the demon realm to confront Everand, ultimately defeating him and freeing Aliza's soul. With her soul restored, Cray and Aliza acknowledged their love for each other.

text:
Professor James Asher and his wife Lydia are once more drawn into the perilous undercurrents of the supernatural. In the year 1908, weary from the administrative burdens of his late relative’s estate, Asher finds himself confronted by an old adversary: Charles Farren, the vampire Earl of Ernchester, who is entangled in a web of conspiracy with the mercenary Ignace Karolyi. As Asher senses the threat, he discreetly follows Farren to Paris, sending a coded message to Lydia, urging her to stay alert.

Lydia, however, is already informed by a cryptic footnote in one of the medical journals she studies—information Asher is unaware of. She discovers that the safe haven Asher plans to reach is not safe at all, infiltrated by a spy aligned with Karolyi. To protect her husband, Lydia turns to Simon Ysidro, the formidable and reclusive head of the London vampires. Ysidro agrees to aid them in thwarting Farren’s ambitions, on one stringent condition: he insists that Lydia’s companion be the rather unassuming yet spirited governess Margaret Potton, whose romantic inclinations may prove as dangerous as any vampire.

With the trio’s journey across Europe underway, Asher joins forces with Anthea, Farren’s powerful and charismatic vampire mate. Their alliance is tested when they reach Constantinople, where Asher himself becomes a target of the city’s vampire lord, who is caught in a bloody power struggle with a rival seeking to destroy him. As Asher vanishes into the city’s shadows, Lydia and Ysidro separately search for clues using Asher’s human contacts and Ysidro’s supernatural senses. Their efforts are complicated by Margaret’s growing fascination with Ysidro and her jealousy toward Lydia, which threatens their unity. It is only by unraveling a tangled series of financial transactions and hunting down a string of gruesome murders that Lydia and Ysidro finally locate Asher and Charles, just in time to flee the city and survive yet another night of terror.

text:
Professor James Asher and his wife Lydia find themselves once more entangled in the perilous world of the undead. It is 1908, and the weary academic, recently returned from the tedium of managing a distant relative’s estate, notices Charles Farren—the vampire Earl of Ernchester—engaged in suspicious dealings with the mercenary Ignace Karolyi. Asher, having left the secret service some years prior to marry Lydia, decides to follow Farren, sensing the threat, and wires a warning to Lydia from the road, unaware of a crucial detail she alone knows.

Lydia, drawing on an obscure medical footnote in one of her journals, realizes the safe haven Asher plans to reach is compromised—its owner is a double agent working for Karolyi. To save her husband, Lydia turns to the oldest vampire in London: the aloof Simon Ysidro. Ysidro agrees to intervene to prevent Farren from forging human alliances, but insists on a risky compromise—he brings along Margaret Potton, a drab but romantic governess, as Lydia’s chaperone against her objections.

The trio tracks Asher across Europe, where Asher joins forces with Farren’s formidable vampire wife, Anthea. In Constantinople, their quest takes a sudden turn when Asher is kidnapped by the city’s vampiric ruler, struggling desperately to maintain power amid mounting threats. While Asher seeks answers to his own uncertain role in the power struggle for his life, Lydia and Ysidro use Asher’s diplomatic contacts and Ysidro’s nocturnal skills to hunt for any trace of him and Charles. Their search grows perilous as Margaret’s infatuation with Ysidro and resentment toward Lydia put everyone at risk.

Only by untangling a maze of financial trails and a string of gruesome murders can Ysidro and Lydia finally locate Asher and Charles—and barely escape the city with their lives intact.
